sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Đi đâu đấy? literally asks where someone is going, but in friendly everyday speech it can work like light small talk after hello. Use it with someone familiar enough for a casual check-in, not as a serious route question to a rushed stranger.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Say Đi đâu đấy? when the conversation already has a friendly tone and the person is visibly heading somewhere.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The phrase is short, but đấy makes it feel conversational.

sections.title: Natural greeting chain
sections.body: This line usually belongs after a greeting, not before one.

phrases.pronunciation: zuht voo ee duhk gap ban

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it with a familiar guide, classmate, host, neighbor, or friendly helper after you have already greeted each other. It fits best when the person is walking out, leaving the desk, or heading toward a visible next place.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Because it can sound personal, keep it for friendly contexts. If you truly need directions from a stranger, ask a direction phrase instead.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: These pages help you choose between small talk and practical directions.
